name: Gawain
summary: The light hauler of the atmospheric tiltrotor pair: lifts 5 t vertically with no runway and cruises it anywhere. Lighter than a V-22 — a proper light EX-class vehicle.
description: EX-2 Gawain is an Efficient-class expeditionary craft (EX). The light hauler of the fleet’s atmospheric tiltrotor pair. It lifts up to 5 t vertically, with no runway, and cruises it to wherever it is needed — any cargo type, to any flat surface. It shares one airframe with the EX-1 Lancelot medic; the two differ in structural gauge, engines, systems, and module fit, not geometry. At its size it is lighter than a V-22 — a genuinely light-class vehicle, not a heavy-lifter.

specs.cruiseSpeed: subsonic transport cruise (below the medic’s Mach 0.75 dash)
specs.modules: 2-slot low bay (1×5 t mono or 2×2.5 t)

components.name: Tilting proprotors
components.what: Shared R 5.75 m rotors; lift in VTOL, cruise as props
components.detail: Same geometry as EX-1; heavier vehicle → higher disk loading (~803 N/m²).

components.name: 2-slot low bay
components.detail: Loads from below onto a flat surface; matches the fleet light-module standard.

capabilities.name: Light vertical hauler
capabilities.detail: Lift up to 5 t vertically and cruise it to any flat surface; lower or release the module. Sized to the common job to keep most flights cheap.

calculations.title: MTOW from shared airframe
calculations.method: Shared EX-1 airframe empty ~9.5 t + 5 t payload + ~2.5 t fuel.
calculations.note: Lighter than a V-22 (27 t) — proper light EX-class.

calculations.title: Hover power scaling
calculations.method: Scale from EX-1 (~2.5 MW at 12 t) by W^1.5.
calculations.note: Disk loading ~803 N/m² on the shared R 5.75 m rotors.

blueprint.frame: Shared EX-1 geometry: fuselage 18.0 m × 2.6 m × 2.4 m; wing span 15 m; rotor tip-to-tip 26.5 m.
blueprint.stations: Same as EX-1 — differs in gauge, engines, systems, module fit, not geometry.

sections.heading: The EX-1 / EX-2 pair
sections.body: One airframe, two roles. At the 5 t size the pairing is honest: a 17 t hauler and a 12 t medic are close enough that a genuinely shared airframe is credible, where a much heavier hauler would have strained the claim.

sections.heading: Why 5 t (not 10 t)
sections.body: The earlier EX-2 was a 31 t / 10 t hauler — heavier than a V-22, violating the EX “small and light” class. Shrinking to 5 t brings it into class, moves it off heavy-lift competitors’ turf, and makes the shared-airframe claim more honest.

changelog.why: A 31 t hauler violated the EX small/light class and overlapped heavy-lift competitors. 5 t is a proper light EX-class vehicle.

decisions.why: Keeps EX-2 in the Efficient class, off heavy-lift turf, and makes the shared-airframe claim credible.
